speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; to begin our assessment, can you describe exactly where you feel the pain and how long it has been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Since your shooting pain occurs when eating and you have difficulty wearing earrings, does the pain radiate to your jaw or temple, and have you noticed any clicking sounds or stiffness in that area?

REQUEST TEST: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) physical exam

speaker: Doctor
text: The TMJ exam results are normal, ruling out jaw muscle tension as the cause. Given your history of chronic ear infections and the specific nature of your shooting pain, have you noticed any drainage from the ear or a sensation of fullness/pressure recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal TMJ exam and your history of recurrent ear infections suggest the pain might be referred from the Eustachian tube or a residual issue from your tympanoplasty. Given the specific trigger of eating and the shooting nature of the pain, have you experienced any changes in your hearing, tinnitus, or a sensation of water trapped in the ear recently?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry (if not current)
REQUEST TEST: Tympanometry

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal audiometry and tympanometry results suggest your tympanic graft is stable and your hearing thresholds are intact. However, the combination of shooting pain triggered by chewing and discomfort with earrings, despite a normal TMJ exam, points toward a specific complication involving the facial nerve. Have you noticed any weakness in your facial muscles, such as difficulty closing your eye on the right side or drooping of the corner of your mouth?

REQUEST TEST: Facial nerve strength assessment (Cranial Nerve VII)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS. Facial Nerve Strength (Cranial Nerve VII): Symmetrical tone and strength bilaterally. No weakness in forehead, eye closure, cheek elevation, or mouth corner symmetry observed.
